root_cause.text: The async_hold queue of encrypted input skbs was not purged in all code paths that call tls_decrypt_async_wait(), specifically when tls_strp_msg_hold() fails part-way through and the decryption falls back to synchronous mode, causing cloned skbs to remain pinned and leak.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "This fixes a leak when tls_strp_msg_hold() fails part-way through, after having added some cloned skbs to the async_hold queue. tls_decrypt_sg() will then call tls_decrypt_async_wait() to process all pending decrypts, and drop back to synchronous mode, but tls_sw_recvmsg() only flushes the async_hold queue when one record has been processed in 'fully-async' mode, which may not be the case here." The patch moves `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold)` from `tls_sw_recvmsg()` into `tls_decrypt_async_wait()` so it is executed unconditionally whenever that function is called.

intent_record.intent_summary: Purge the async_hold skb queue in tls_decrypt_async_wait to prevent memory leaks and ensure clean state after waiting for async decryption.
intent_record.what: Added a call to __skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold) in the function tls_decrypt_async_wait, which removes and frees all skbs in the async_hold queue before returning.
intent_record.how: At runtime, before returning from tls_decrypt_async_wait, any skbs still held in the async_hold queue are now purged (freed). Previously, these skbs would remain in the queue, potentially causing memory leaks or stale entries in subsequent operations.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix a potential use-after-free or double-free by removing the premature purging of the async hold queue after async decryption wait in tls_sw_recvmsg.
intent_record.what: Removed the call to `__skb_queue_purge(&ctx->async_hold);` from the `tls_sw_recvmsg` function after waiting for async decryption to complete.
intent_record.how: The change removes an unconditional purge of the async hold queue after all previously submitted decryption operations have finished. This means the queue is no longer emptied at this point, which could affect memory handling and might prevent a potential use-after-free or double-free issue if the buffers were still referenced elsewhere.

grouping_result.intent: Purge the async_hold skb queue in tls_decrypt_async_wait to prevent memory leaks and ensure clean state after waiting for async decryption.
Fix a potential use-after-free or double-free by removing the premature purging of the async hold queue after async decryption wait in tls_sw_recvmsg.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly addresses the root cause by purging the async_hold skb queue in tls_decrypt_async_wait, which is the missing cleanup that leads to skb leaks when decryption falls back to synchronous mode.

The root cause describes missing purges of the async hold queue in certain code paths, leading to leaks. Group 1 removes a premature purge to fix a use-after-free, which addresses a different issue and does not directly address the missing purges described in the vulnerability.

candidates.rationale: This line initiates waiting for async decryption but does not purge the async_hold queue afterwards, allowing skbs to remain pinned and leak.
Incrementing decrypt_pending is part of the async flow, but without purging the async_hold queue, pending skbs are not cleaned up, leading to leaks.
This return statement exits the function without purging the async_hold skb queue, directly causing the memory leak when decryption falls back to synchronous mode.

Incrementing decrypt_pending is part of the async flow, but without purging the async_hold queue, pending skbs are not cleaned up, leading to leaks when tls_strp_msg_hold() fails and synchronous fallback occurs.
This return statement exits the function without purging the async_hold skb queue, directly causing the memory leak when decryption falls back to synchronous mode after a failed tls_strp_msg_hold().
